title: Knowledge check: Understanding the jQuery Ecosystem

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of understanding the jquery ecosystem?
options: jQuery is a JavaScript library that wraps common DOM, event, effect, and request tasks in a concise, chainable API. It complements JavaScript rather than replacing it.
Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.
Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
questions.answer_key: jQuery is a JavaScript library that wraps common DOM, event, effect, and request tasks in a concise, chainable API. It complements JavaScript rather than replacing it.
questions.explanation: jQuery is a JavaScript library that wraps common DOM, event, effect, and request tasks in a concise, chainable API. It complements JavaScript rather than replacing it. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which check is most useful after trying jquery core?
options: Assume the first attempt succeeded and skip verification.
Use jquery core deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
Use a removed jQuery API as the default for new code.
Bind another global handler after every render without cleanup.
questions.answer_key: Use jquery core deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.explanation: A focused observation checks behavior rather than assuming the method call guarantees the intended result. Include an edge case when the state or inputs can vary.

questions.prompt: Which verification approach best supports professional work with understanding the jquery ecosystem?
options: Move answer keys and private configuration into frontend code.
Test only the first render and publish immediately.
Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
Replace all native browser APIs with jQuery whether needed or not.
questions.answer_key: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.explanation: Expected-versus-actual checks, relevant edge cases, and recorded limitations make the implementation easier to debug and review.
